text:
maria: ran the 100k request perf sweep on staging, attaching pprof + flame. p99 jumps from 110ms -> 520ms when KV miss rate hits ~18% and kernel flips.
devon: can you paste the flame or the top stack? curious where the extra 400ms is.
maria: top of flame shows `kv_fetch_sync` + `select_kernel_dyn()` + CUDA memcpy stalls. gist: https://redwood-gists/pprof/1965432100
lee: thats the old sync prefetch path. iirc we still do synchronous KV fetch for microbatch<8.
sanjay: microbatch size used for the sweep?
maria: microbatch=4 for latency SLO testing. We wanted lower p95 but maybe getting p99 tail.
devon: hypothesis: small microbatch -> more frequent kernel selection -> more kernel cache misses -> kernel churn -> device context switches and memcpy thrash.
lee: agreed. when we up microbatch to 8, throughput improves and kernel flips less often but p95 slightly up. p99 drops in our test.
sanjay: what's the GPU util at microbatch=4 vs 8?
maria: util@4 ~72% avg but very spiky (p99 util ~98%). @8 util avg~85% p99~90%.
devon: sounds like headroom strategy is failing: we wanted target util 70% to avoid spikes. but async prefetch could smooth it.
lee: i ran a profile with async prefetch enabled (experimental) — KV misses are overlapped with compute, memcpy reduced by ~45%. p99 improved by ~160ms.
maria: nice. code change is tiny:
```
// enable async kv prefetch when microbatch < 8
cfg.prefetch.async = true
cfg.prefetch.window = 2
```
devon: window=2 ok? We might need to tune for sequence length variance.
sanjay: also need admission control tweak: when estimated util > 85% we should start shedding non-critical low-priority routes instead of allowing kernel flips.
lee: +1 on route-based shedding. we can add a quick heuristic: estimate_kv_miss_rate * batch_rate -> expected extra memcpy time -> if predicted p99 > slo then shed.
maria: can we simulate that with the loadgen? i'll add a synthetic p95/p99 observer to the RL simulator.
devon: ping me if you need custom kernels in the trace to model kernel-flip penalty.
infra-bot: deploy queued: canary to staging with async prefetch flag ON. build/6821 -> staging (maria).
sanjay: one more thought — quantization/kernel choice also affects flip cost. switching to the int8 path for short sequences reduced kernel size but increased memcpy for larger KV entries. tradeoff matrix next sprint.
maria: action items: 1) run sim with async prefetch + microbatch 4/6/8 to map p95/p99/throughput curve (maria) 2) implement admission heuristic for route-level shedding (lee) 3) add kernel-flip penalty tunable to trace generator (devon) 4) perf note for quantized kernels (sanjay). i'll upload pprof artifacts to the perf board.
lee: i'll start a small canary run for microbatch=6 after staging looks stable.
devon: we should record results in the perf-run sheet and mark any rollback criteria. p99 > 250ms => rollback.
maria: ack. starting sims now, will post results in this thread. :mag:
